ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A horizontal conveyor belt with a length $L_{AB} = 10\mathrm{m}$ rotates clockwise at a speed of $v = 1\mathrm{m/s}$. A student gently places a small block of mass $m = 0.04\mathrm{kg}$ at the far left end of the conveyor belt. Simultaneously, another student fires a pellet of mass $m_0 = 0.01\mathrm{kg}$ from a toy gun. The pellet embeds itself into the small block, and the interaction time is extremely short. It is known that the instantaneous velocity of the pellet just before hitting the small block is parallel to the conveyor belt with a magnitude of $v_0 = 35\mathrm{m/s}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the small block and the conveyor belt is $\mu = 0.3$. Both the block and the pellet can be treated as point masses, and $g = 10\mathrm{m/s}^2$ is used.

1. What is the speed of the small slider after the collision with the projectile?
2. What is the time it takes for the small block to move from point A to point B?

Above the conveyor belt there is an arrow v pointing to the right, indicating that the upper surface moves to the right. The gun and projectile m0 are on the left side of the block, and the projectile will shoot into the block to the right along the horizontal direction. Therefore take the right direction from A to B as the positive direction, the initial velocity of the projectile is +35 m/s, and the conveyor belt velocity is +1 m/s. Reasoning: The collision time is extremely short, ignore the impulse of friction during the collision process, and momentum in the horizontal direction is conserved. The block is initially approximately at rest, and after the projectile embeds into the block, their common velocity is V = m0 v0 / (m + m0) = 0.01 × 35 / (0.04 + 0.01) = 7 m/s. So the velocity of the slider after collision is 7 m/s, directed to the right. After collision, the velocity of the combined body 7 m/s is greater than the conveyor belt velocity 1 m/s, so it slides to the right relative to the conveyor belt, the kinetic friction force is to the left, and the acceleration a = -μg = -0.3 × 10 = -3 m/s². The time required for the velocity to decrease from 7 m/s to 1 m/s is t1 = (1 - 7) / (-3) = 2 s. The displacement in this process is s1 = (7 + 1)/2 × 2 = 8 m. The total length of the conveyor belt AB = 10 m, and 2 m remains. After that, the block is relatively at rest with the conveyor belt and moves to the right at 1 m/s, and the required time is t2 = 2 / 1 = 2 s. The total time t = t1 + t2 = 4 s.

Treat the embedding collision as instantaneous, so external friction impulse is negligible and horizontal momentum is conserved: V=(m0 v0)/(m+m0). After getting V=7 m/s, compare it with the belt speed 1 m/s. Since the combined block-pellet is faster than the belt, kinetic friction acts leftward with acceleration a=-mu g=-3 m/s^2 until its ground speed drops to 1 m/s. Use constant-acceleration kinematics to find the slowing time and distance, then move the remaining distance at the belt speed after no slipping. This gives the collision speed and total travel time.

method.method_draft: First read the image: the upper belt run moves right from A toward B, and the pellet approaches the block horizontally from the left, so the projectile and belt directions are the same. From the text read the same masses, speeds, length, friction coefficient, and g. Solve using the conveyor-belt frame, which is inertial because the belt speed is constant. In that frame, before impact the pellet speed is 35-1=34 m/s and the gently placed block has speed 0-1=-1 m/s. Conserve horizontal momentum for the perfectly inelastic collision in this moving frame to obtain the post-collision relative-to-belt speed: u=[m0(34)+m(-1)]/(m+m0)=6 m/s, equivalent to 7 m/s in the ground frame. During sliding, friction reduces this relative speed to zero with acceleration magnitude mu g=3 m/s^2. Compute the relative stopping time and relative slip distance; add the belt-carried displacement during that same time to get the ground displacement before sticking to the belt. Then cover the remaining distance to B at 1 m/s.

raw_record.original_question:
A horizontal conveyor belt with a length $L_{AB} = 10\mathrm{m}$ rotates clockwise at a speed of $v = 1\mathrm{m/s}$. A student gently places a small block of mass $m = 0.04\mathrm{kg}$ at the far left end of the conveyor belt. Simultaneously, another student fires a pellet of mass $m_0 = 0.01\mathrm{kg}$ from a toy gun. The pellet embeds itself into the small block, and the interaction time is extremely short. It is known that the instantaneous velocity of the pellet just before hitting the small block is parallel to the conveyor belt with a magnitude of $v_0 = 35\mathrm{m/s}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the small block and the conveyor belt is $\mu = 0.3$. Both the block and the pellet can be treated as point masses, and $g = 10\mathrm{m/s}^2$ is used.

1. What is the speed of the small slider after the collision with the projectile?
2. What is the time it takes for the small block to move from point A to point B?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the conveyor belt is placed horizontally, the left end is labeled A, and the right end is labeled B; the small block m is located near the left end A above the conveyor belt. Above the conveyor belt there is an arrow v pointing to the right, indicating that the upper surface moves to the right. The gun and projectile m0 are on the left side of the block, and the projectile will shoot into the block to the right along the horizontal direction. Therefore take the right direction from A to B as the positive direction, the initial velocity of the projectile is +35 m/s, and the conveyor belt velocity is +1 m/s.

Reasoning: The collision time is extremely short, ignore the impulse of friction during the collision process, and momentum in the horizontal direction is conserved. The block is initially approximately at rest, and after the projectile embeds into the block, their common velocity is V = m0 v0 / (m + m0) = 0.01 × 35 / (0.04 + 0.01) = 7 m/s. So the velocity of the slider after collision is 7 m/s, directed to the right.

After collision, the velocity of the combined body 7 m/s is greater than the conveyor belt velocity 1 m/s, so it slides to the right relative to the conveyor belt, the kinetic friction force is to the left, and the acceleration a = -μg = -0.3 × 10 = -3 m/s². The time required for the velocity to decrease from 7 m/s to 1 m/s is t1 = (1 - 7) / (-3) = 2 s. The displacement in this process is s1 = (7 + 1)/2 × 2 = 8 m. The total length of the conveyor belt AB = 10 m, and 2 m remains. After that, the block is relatively at rest with the conveyor belt and moves to the right at 1 m/s, and the required time is t2 = 2 / 1 = 2 s. The total time t = t1 + t2 = 4 s.
